title: Sake instead of vodka; playing in Japan
summary: He prefers sake and praises Japanese audiences.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Excuse me while I have a sip of my favorite as of now. It has replaced vodka. Because vodka turns me
into Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde -- I become Mr. Hyde. But sake is easy on you.
They are a very civilized people, and I love them. I know a lot of Japanese; also the language I know quite a bit of.
You have been there a number of times, haven't you?

I've only been over there twice. And both times... The second time I was over there, I really enjoyed myself. I think they are beautiful people. They're so courteous and appreciative. They don't applaud until everything is all over, and then you just barely hear a little, and you look up... When you're putting your music away, you look up and they're all gone. But you know they've been there.
